ancestry-deep-dwarf.markdown:
# Deep Dwarf

*Grey skin, great watchful eyes and a quiet step beneath the weight of the world.*

The ancestors of Deep Dwarves went farther down. Over long generations, the people of the depths became shorter and slighter than their surface cousins. Their skin ranges through shades of grey, and their large eyes gather the faint light of the underground. Narrow shoulders and economical movements suit passages where a broad surface dwarf would struggle.

Many are naturally shy. They watch before approaching, speak after listening and prefer a familiar companion to the attention of a crowded room. Reserve does not diminish curiosity, courage or conviction. A quiet Deep Dwarf may be the first to notice danger and the one who refuses to abandon a friend.

Stone, darkness and small changes in air or vibration shape their experience. Those raised above ground bring the same sensitive bodies to unfamiliar surroundings. No ancestral instinct supplies a map of tunnels they have never walked.

## Rules

Choose two of the five traits below. Temperamental tendencies are invitations, not a required personality. Any ancestry may grow up in any culture. Only the printed rules grant mechanical benefits.

**Starting values:** HP +2; base Speed 5.

- [Eyes for the Dark](trait-deep-dwarf-eyes-for-the-dark.md) — You study the passage in a faint wash of reflected light.
- [The Stone Tells You](trait-deep-dwarf-stone-tells-you.md) — You rest your palm against the floor and wait for the answering tread.
- [A Sense of Depth](trait-deep-dwarf-never-off-the-map.md) — You wake in the dark and know which wall lies beneath the mountain.
- [A Patient Breath](trait-deep-dwarf-holds-its-own.md) — You slow your breathing while the others hurry through the stale passage.
- [Through the Narrow Places](trait-deep-dwarf-where-tall-folk-cannot-stand.md) — You lower your head and slip beneath the fallen beam without breaking stride.

**Starting coin contribution:** +2 coins. See [starting coins](../starting-coins.md).

**Status:** Prepared for v16.7.0 under Bruce’s release instruction; trait approvals recorded separately.

ancestry-dwarf.markdown:
# Hill Dwarf

*Broad shoulders, patient hands and a home made where mountain meets open sky.*

Long ago, dwarven peoples took different roads. Some built their halls within mountains opening onto the surface world. Others traveled deeper into the earth. Centuries of separation, perhaps much longer, have left their descendants visibly different.

Hill Dwarves are the broad, stocky surface people: solid limbs, strong backs, dense hair and faces weathered by forge heat, mountain wind or ordinary years of work. Their halls connect stone interiors to roads, daylight and neighboring communities. Deep Dwarves are their distant kin, but a stranger would seldom mistake one for the other.

Endurance, craft and a lasting memory are familiar expressions of Hill Dwarf identity. A remembered debt may be a kindness worth returning as readily as an injury worth answering. A dwarf need not live in a mountain, work a forge or keep a grudge; the same steady body can belong to a sailor, gardener or traveling musician.

## Rules

Choose two of the five traits below. Temperamental tendencies are invitations, not a required personality. Any ancestry may grow up in any culture. Only the printed rules grant mechanical benefits.

**Starting values:** HP +4; base Speed 5.

- [Hard as Bedrock](trait-dwarf-deep-constitution.md) — Your ancestors did not dig a home from the mountain by yielding politely.
- [Stone Mason](trait-dwarf-stone-reader.md) — You know a mason’s lie by the stone around it.
- [Rooted in Stone](trait-dwarf-low-center.md) — Let the storm waste its strength on you.
- [An Honest Maker’s Hand](trait-dwarf-maker-s-eye.md) — Your thumb finds the seam; your ear knows the ring of sound metal.
- [A Grudge Well Kept](trait-dwarf-carved-history.md) — You remember who struck first. You intend them to remember what followed.

**Starting coin contribution:** +2 coins. See [starting coins](../starting-coins.md).

**Status:** Prepared for v16.7.0 under Bruce’s release instruction; trait approvals recorded separately.

ancestry-elf.markdown:
# Wood Elf

*Short, dark-haired and quick; the next possibility is already tugging at your sleeve.*

Wood Elves are shorter and more lightly built than High Elves, with dark hair, nimble limbs and expressive, angular faces. Similar ears and facial structures have given both peoples the name elf in other tongues. A Wood Elf watching a High Elf deliberate may wonder how anyone can bear to leave an interesting idea untried for so long.

Quick movement often accompanies quick feeling. Curiosity, anger and affection can arrive with equal force; many Wood Elves trust the first useful opening and discover its consequences afterward. Their rashness can become daring, and their impulsiveness can become generosity. Neither prevents a Wood Elf from learning patience or taking a promise seriously.

Their bodies lend themselves to balance and movement. Woodlands give those gifts abundant expression, but a Wood Elf raised among rooftops, ships or crowded streets remains a Wood Elf. Their community determines what those quick hands learn to do.

## Rules

Choose two of the five traits below. Temperamental tendencies are invitations, not a required personality. Any ancestry may grow up in any culture. Only the printed rules grant mechanical benefits.

**Starting values:** HP +2; base Speed 6.

- [Footfall on the Leaves](trait-elf-light-tread.md) — Even the fallen leaves seem reluctant to betray your passing.
- [A Lifetime Ago](trait-elf-age-of-memory.md) — You remember when the old road was new.
- [Nature’s Whispers](trait-elf-leaf-listener.md) — A startled bird tells you what a shouted warning never could.
- [Grace of the Elder Folk](trait-elf-unhurried-grace.md) — Where others hurry, you seem simply to arrive.
- [Dream beneath the Stars](trait-elf-star-familiar.md) — Your body rests while part of you walks old paths.

**Starting coin contribution:** +2 coins. See [starting coins](../starting-coins.md).

**Status:** Prepared for v16.7.0 under Bruce’s release instruction; trait approvals recorded separately.

ancestry-gnome.markdown:
# Gnome

*Tiny fey bodies, long lives and minds forever asking what else a thing could become.*

Gnomes are fey creatures, smaller even than halflings, with deft hands, keen senses and an intelligence that can make a complicated device seem almost embarrassingly obvious. Their faces carry the expressions of long experience, however easily a stranger mistakes their stature for youth.

Some say the gnomes left the world of fairie to explore possibilities its inhabitants had overlooked. Others insist they were thrown out, and disagree enthusiastically about what invention caused the trouble. Gnomes tell both stories. Whether anyone remembers the whole truth is another question.

Inventing and tinkering delight many gnomes: an unfamiliar mechanism invites examination, an accepted limitation invites an experiment. Others apply that same searching intelligence to music, medicine, argument or the behavior of friends. A gnome does not inherit a workshop or a profession. Their fey nature and extraordinary mind travel with them wherever they grow up.

## Rules

Choose two of the five traits below. Temperamental tendencies are invitations, not a required personality. Any ancestry may grow up in any culture. Only the printed rules grant mechanical benefits.

**Starting values:** HP +1; base Speed 6; Size Small.

- [What’s It Made Of?](trait-gnome-whats-it-made-of.md) — You turn the device over, already asking why its maker put the hinge there.
- [Eyes from Elsewhere](trait-gnome-one-more-question.md) — The painted door is convincing. Its shadow has forgotten where the sun is.
- [Fingers in the Works](trait-gnome-fingers-in-the-works.md) — You ease one small part out of place, and the whole machine loses its argument.
- [Small Target](trait-gnome-small-target.md) — You tuck yourself behind the low stone as the arrow strikes its edge.
- [Bright Idea](trait-gnome-bright-idea.md) — You draw three lines in the dust, add a spoon, and the answer takes shape.

**Starting coin contribution:** +1 coins. See [starting coins](../starting-coins.md).

**Status:** Prepared for v16.7.0 under Bruce’s release instruction; trait approvals recorded separately.

ancestry-goblin.markdown:
# Goblin

*Quick hands, shared effort and a future finally open to your own making.*

Goblins are small, quick-bodied people with prominent ears and alert, expressive faces. For generations, orcs enslaved them, and outsiders learned to associate goblins with the cruelty of those who held them. Freedom did not immediately erase that reputation. It did give goblins the chance to build lives whose purpose was their own.

Many now seek a place through useful work, trade, exploration and the steady proof of being a reliable neighbor. Resourcefulness honed under deprivation can become skilled repair, careful husbandry or a gift for seeing value where others see rubbish. Cooperation can become friendship and enterprise rather than a necessity of survival.

A goblin adventurer may want to support a community, win recognition or simply discover what freedom feels like beyond familiar roads. Others were born free and have never seen an orc. Their ancestry carries a history; each goblin chooses what to make of the life ahead.

## Rules

Choose two of the five traits below. Temperamental tendencies are invitations, not a required personality. Any ancestry may grow up in any culture. Only the printed rules grant mechanical benefits.

**Starting values:** HP +1; base Speed 6; Size Small.

- [Waste Nothing](trait-goblin-scavenger.md) — You turn the broken hinge over. There is good work left in it yet.
- [Better Together](trait-goblin-more-of-us-than-you.md) — Your companion draws their eye, and you know exactly when to step in.
- [Quick on Your Feet](trait-goblin-run-away-better.md) — You are halfway across the yard before the others have found their stride.
- [The Other Side of the Fire](trait-goblin-other-side-of-the-fire.md) — You recognize the guarded silence and make your offer without stepping closer.
- [Quick Hands](trait-goblin-never-where-you-aim.md) — The awkward bundle settles into your grip before anyone notices it slipping.

ancestry-halfling.markdown:
# Halfling

*Quiet feet, a generous table and courage that surprises people who judge by height.*

Halflings are small, compact people, larger than gnomes, with a gift for making limited space comfortable. Others often notice their height before noticing the person, a mistake a halfling may patiently correct or quietly put to use.

Hospitality and good company are familiar pleasures, but a generous table does not require an easy life. Courage can live beside trembling knees, a sharp tongue beside warm manners, and a taste for home beside an irresistible curiosity about the road. A halfling raised far from halfling communities brings their own customs to those possibilities.

## Rules

Choose two of the five traits below. These are invitations to a familiar fantasy,
not a required personality. Any ancestry may grow up in any culture.

**Starting values:** HP +1; base Speed 5; Size Small.

- [Bigger on the Inside](trait-halfling-stout-heart.md) — Your knees may shake. Your friends will never see you leave them.
- [Under Their Noses](trait-halfling-small-passage.md) — The grand folk rarely remember to look beneath the table.
- [Quick Tongue](trait-halfling-quiet-company.md) — You can talk your way through a negotiation, an argument or an accusation.
- [A Little Luck](trait-halfling-good-cheer.md) — The latch catches your coat a heartbeat before you step into trouble.
- [Endless Pockets](trait-halfling-resilient.md) — Your clothes have pockets in places that should not have pockets, and they hold more than they should.

ancestry-high-elf.markdown:
# High Elf

*Tall, strong and deliberate; a long life leaves room to consider every word.*

High Elves are tall and strongly built, with pointed ears and the fine, angular facial structure that leads outsiders to call them kin to Wood Elves. They are a different ancestry. Beside a compact, restless Wood Elf, a High Elf has the presence of a standing stone: upright, composed and difficult to hurry.

Their long lives encourage a broad view of consequences. Many listen through an argument before speaking, practice a movement until it wastes no effort, or remember a slight long after its author has forgotten it. Confidence can harden into arrogance, especially when patience is mistaken for superior judgment. Others learn that living a long time is no guarantee of being right.

A High Elf might be a laborer, a wanderer or a scholar. Strength and deliberation belong to their physical and temperamental inheritance; wealth, titles and courtly manners depend on the life they have led.

## Rules

Choose two of the five traits below. Temperamental tendencies are invitations, not a required personality. Any ancestry may grow up in any culture. Only the printed rules grant mechanical benefits.

**Starting values:** HP +3; base Speed 6.

- [The Practised Hand](trait-high-elf-practised-hand.md) — You turn the tiny fitting once, then set it exactly where it belongs.
- [Still Water](trait-high-elf-old-courtesies.md) — You let the clamor spend itself before deciding what deserves your attention.
- [Starlight Eyes](trait-high-elf-starlight-eyes.md) — Under the last light of evening, you can still count the stitches.
- [Measured Strength](trait-high-elf-name-that-opens-doors.md) — You set your feet, test the weight and lift without a wasted motion.
- [The Weight of Centuries](trait-high-elf-weight-of-centuries.md) — You close your eyes, and the room returns as it stood a lifetime ago.

ancestry-human.markdown:
# Human

*Restless, adaptable and fiercely invested in a life that never feels long enough.*

Humans have no single stature, complexion or way of making a home. A short life beside the elder peoples can give an ordinary season an urgent importance: learn the trade, mend the friendship, see what lies beyond the ridge. Some make roots; others make roads between the places they love.

Adaptability takes many forms. One human gathers languages and acquaintances; another learns by failing until a stubborn problem yields. Neither ambition nor restlessness is compulsory. A human hero may want a quiet life enough to undertake a dangerous journey to protect it.

## Rules

Choose two of the five traits below. These are invitations to a familiar fantasy,
not a required personality. Any ancestry may grow up in any culture.

**Starting values:** HP +2; base Speed 6.

- [Never Quite Finished](trait-human-weathered.md) — There is always one more person to help, one more hill to cross.
- [Adaptable](trait-human-far-walker.md) — You learn quickly, turning every new experience into another useful skill.
- [A Foot in Two Worlds](trait-human-many-homes.md) — You learned early that a stranger is sometimes only a person whose words you do not know.
- [Ingenuity](trait-human-shared-table.md) — You look at what is available and build the tool you need.
- [The Impossible Streak](trait-human-practiced-patience.md) — Someone says it cannot be done, and you hear a challenge.

**Starting coin contribution:** +1 coins. See [starting coins](../starting-coins.md).

ancestry-oath-bound.markdown:
# Oath-Bound

*Made for a purpose. Set adrift before you learned what it was.*

Oath-Bound are constructs brought into existence by an oath holder. Each was made for a higher purpose and carries a destiny, yet begins their life without knowing what that purpose or destiny is. They have been given existence without an explanation: a ship set adrift, with neither a chart nor a remembered destination.

Their oath holder is the source of that existence. An Oath-Bound may recognize a name, a presence or a sign of the one who made them. Calling upon that connection can bring conviction, understanding or strength. The answer may feel intimate even when the being who gives it remains a mystery.

Life among other peoples gives them relationships, work and ambitions of their own. A journey might uncover why they were made, or simply teach them what they value while searching. The character’s choices belong to the player; their hidden purpose offers a mystery to discover together with the Dungeon Architect.

## Rules

Choose two of the five traits below. Temperamental tendencies are invitations, not a required personality. Any ancestry may grow up in any culture. Only the printed rules grant mechanical benefits.

**Starting values:** HP +2; base Speed 6.

**Constructed life:** Use the shared [Oath-Bound recovery rules](../rules/ancestry-procedures.md).

- [The Answering Voice](trait-oath-bound-the-mark.md) — You reach toward the presence that made you, and certainty settles into your voice.
- [Borrowed Knowing](trait-oath-bound-read-the-oath.md) — You know the answer before you know where the memory came from.
- [The Debt Comes Due](trait-oath-bound-the-debt-comes-due.md) — You ask for another chance, and a little of the life you were given answers.
- [The Will That Made You](trait-oath-bound-bound-by-your-word.md) — Something in you remembers that your work is unfinished.
- [A Hand on the Rudder](trait-oath-bound-neither-here-nor-there.md) — For a moment, the world is less bewildering and the next step feels clearer.

**Starting coin contribution:** +1 coins. See [starting coins](../starting-coins.md).

**Status:** Prepared for v16.7.0 under Bruce’s release instruction; trait approvals recorded separately.

ancestry-tallfolk.markdown:
# Tallfolk

*Long limbs, great hands and a world whose doorways rarely give you room.*

Tallfolk stand well above most neighboring peoples. Long arms, powerful frames and large hands make their scale evident even when they sit quietly. A borrowed chair, a crowded wagon or a low lintel can demand more thought than a heavy load.

Some enjoy the attention their height brings; others become practiced at folding themselves out of the way. Their bodies offer reach and leverage, but neither strength nor stature decides their character. A Tallfolk healer may work with extraordinary gentleness, while a shy scholar learns to endure being the first person everyone notices.

Their origins and communities belong to the campaign. They need no named giant ancestor or distant kingdom to take their place beside other adventurers. Choose how your hero lives at this scale, and which of its advantages they have learned to use.

## Rules

Choose two of the five traits below. Temperamental tendencies are invitations, not a required personality. Any ancestry may grow up in any culture. Only the printed rules grant mechanical benefits.

**Starting values:** HP +5; base Speed 6.

- [Long Reach](trait-tallfolk-long-reach.md) — You catch the latch above your companions’ heads without rising onto your toes.
- [Broad Back](trait-tallfolk-broad-back.md) — You settle the awkward load across your shoulders and leave a hand free for the door.
- [A Big Shadow](trait-tallfolk-a-big-shadow.md) — You unfold to your full height, and wait for the room to notice.
- [Built for the Weather](trait-tallfolk-built-for-the-weather.md) — You pull your collar closed and keep pace through the driving sleet.
- [Long Stride](trait-tallfolk-you-take-the-blow.md) — You cross the courtyard in a few easy strides while your companions hurry to keep pace.

*Roll Knowledge to fire a folding launcher that damages and pushes creatures in a line of three squares.*

- **Standard:** 5 physical damage; push 2 squares away from you.
- **Strong:** 7 physical damage; push 3 squares away from you.

The launcher folds back into your hands after firing.

**Equipment / acquisition:** One reusable folding launcher (Bulk 1), built on learning and supplied if needed.

rule-vision.markdown:
# Vision and perception

Light and perception determine what a hero can observe and target. An ability grants the sense, rating or range it names; use the shared definitions here to resolve it.

## Light and sight

In complete darkness, no one can see.

In low light, the Dungeon Architect assigns 1 to 3 Banes according to the level of darkness. Apply these Banes to observation attempts and actions that require vision.

| Illumination | Sight-related Banes |
|---|---:|
| Clear light | 0 |
| Dim light | 1 |
| Very dim light | 2 |
| Barely perceptible light | 3 |

The table gives guidance for describing a lighting penalty. Judge the light reaching the subject of the attempt and apply that penalty once to the roll. Other sources of Boons and Banes use the ordinary resolution rules.

## Low-Light Vision

Low-Light Vision has a rating. Ignore that many Banes imposed by low light, to a minimum of zero low-light Banes. Remove the ignored lighting Banes before combining the roll’s remaining Boons and Banes.

For example, in light imposing 3 Banes, Low-Light Vision 1 leaves 2 low-light Banes. Low-Light Vision 2 leaves 1. In complete darkness, no one can see.

## Seismic Vision

While touching a continuous solid surface, Seismic Vision lets you pinpoint moving creatures and objects touching that surface within the sense’s printed range. It works in complete darkness.

You may use this perception to target a creature or object it locates. Use the attack’s or ability’s ordinary range and require a clear path to the target.

For example, a Deep Dwarf with The Stone Tells You can pinpoint a creature moving across the same connected stone floor within 6 squares, even after the lantern goes out. They can target that creature with an ability whose range and clear path reach it.

## Other forms of perception

Sonar, seismic, thermal and spiritual perception are distinct forms of perception. A named sense uses its own means of gathering information. Its rules state what it perceives and how that information supports observation and targeting; its granting ability supplies any printed range.

rule-ancestry-procedures.markdown:
# Reach, defense and recovery

Ancestry traits use the ordinary action, targeting and recovery procedures together with their printed grants.

## Touch and object interactions

Ordinary physical reach extends to an adjacent square. A touch ability is one whose rules or narrative require contact with its target. An ability’s printed adjacency requirement describes distance; its description establishes whether it uses physical contact.

An explicit reach grant gives its printed distance for the interactions it names. Long Reach gives Tallfolk a range of 2 squares for object interactions and non-attack touch abilities. Use the ordinary action cost each time: picking up an object costs a Maneuver, and a touch ability spends its printed action and costs. Attack range follows the attack’s printed rules.

For example, a Tallfolk with Long Reach can pick up a key 2 squares away with a Maneuver, or use a healing touch ability on an ally 2 squares away. Each use follows its ordinary action cost.

## Defense Boons when the attacker rolls

When the defender rolls, apply defense Boons and Banes to that defense roll. When a player-controlled attacker makes the roll instead, each applicable defense Boon becomes 1 Bane to the attack, and each applicable defense Bane becomes 1 Boon to the attack. Combine those with the attacker’s own Boons and Banes normally.

For example, Small Target gives a gnome 1 Boon to defense rolls. Against an attack rolled by another player, that benefit instead supplies 1 Bane to the attacker’s roll.

## Oath-Bound recovery

Oath-Bound count as living creatures for healing and use the ordinary hero rules for HP, wounds, rest and recovery.

## Paying HP costs

When an ability asks you to spend HP, pay its printed amount. This cost bypasses resistance and must leave you with at least 1 HP.

## HP unavailable for recovery

When an ability makes spent HP unavailable for recovery until a stated time, record that HP and its release time. During that period, healing and a safe breath can restore HP up to maximum HP minus the unavailable amount. Record this separately from wounds and maximum HP.

For example, an Oath-Bound with maximum HP 20 uses The Debt Comes Due and spends 1 HP. Until the next dawn, healing or a safe breath can restore them to 19 HP. At dawn, that HP becomes available for ordinary recovery again.

A reroll replaces the original roll for the same action or event. Use the original attribute and applicable Boons and Banes, roll again, and resolve the new result, including its retained natural dice.
